Subject: SOC2 Type II + scope question for private/VPC deployments

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — Acme Health is evaluating Redwood for several internal AI use cases. Our security team has a couple of asks before we can proceed: we need a copy of Redwood's latest SOC 2 Type II report (audit period) and confirmation on whether the SOC 2 coverage applies to your Private (customer VPC / on-prem) deployment model.

Specifically:
- Can you share the most recent SOC 2 Type II report and the audit period it covers?
- For Private (VPC/on-prem) customers where the control plane is customer-managed, is that deployment in-scope of Redwood's SOC 2? If not, what evidence or attestation can you provide for controls relevant to the product features we use?
- If you can provide a short bridge letter covering the gap from the report end date to today, that would be helpful.

We have an external auditor (AuditCorp) coordinating evidence collection — cc'd is our procurement mailbox who will track the artifacts. Can you confirm next steps and an ETA?

Thanks,
Jordan Reed
Security Programs
Acme Health

Hi Jordan — thanks for the note and great meeting yesterday.

Short answers up front:
- We can share our most recent SOC 2 Type II report and provide a bridge letter for the period up to the current date.
- Hosted (Redwood-managed) and Dedicated (Redwood-managed reserved capacity) deployments are covered under our SOC 2 Type II scope.
- Private deployments (customer-managed VPC/on-prem) are typically out-of-scope for controls that depend on customer-managed infrastructure. That said, we can provide control mappings, design documentation, and where applicable, evidentiary artifacts for Redwood-managed components (control plane integrations, API auth, encryption-at-rest keys managed by Redwood).

I’m looping in Laura (security) and Mina (compliance) to provide the formal guidance, the SOC 2 PDF, and the bridge letter. Expect a follow-up with attachments and a short scoped guidance doc.

Next steps we propose:
1) We’ll upload the SOC2 report and bridge letter to a shared Drive folder and send a link.
2) We’ll attach a one-page scope matrix that enumerates which control categories remain covered for Private deployments vs what the customer must attest to.
3) If AuditCorp needs an evidence index or direct intake, we can arrange a secure artifact share or a timestamped CSV with evidence pointers.

ETA: Laura/Mina — can you confirm and send the report + guidance today?

Thanks,

Hi Jordan — thanks for the clear ask. I’m Laura (Head of Security, Redwood). I’ve attached the SOC 2 Type II and a short guidance PDF that explains how scope maps to each deployment model. We also included an evidence index CSV to help AuditCorp locate artifacts quickly.

Summary (short):
- Audit period: 2024-10-01 to 2025-09-30 (SOC 2 Type II).
- Bridge letter: we provide a dated bridge letter that attests to the absence of material control changes since the report end date; attached is a draft bridge letter dated 2025-11-06.
- Deployment scope: Hosted (API endpoints & managed infra) — in-scope. Dedicated (Redwood-managed reserved GPU pools) — in-scope (same control boundary as hosted). Private (customer-managed VPC or on-prem) — out-of-scope for infrastructure controls that rely on customer-managed networking, host, or KMS.

What we can provide for Private deployments:
- Control mappings showing which SOC 2 controls remain in effect (application auth, RBAC, audit logging for Redwood-managed services, TLS for in-transit).
- Design docs for the Redwood agent/connector that runs in-customer VPC and the APIs it calls.
- Configuration checklists we recommend customers complete to satisfy infrastructure controls (network hardening, host patching, customer KMS rotation policies).
- Time-stamped evidence pointers for Redwood-managed controls (e.g., logs, RBAC policy snapshots, release notes).

Attachments included (uploaded to shared Drive):
- Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2024-10-01_to_2025-09-30.pdf (PDF, final)
- SOC2_Private_Deployment_Scope_Guidance.pdf (one-page matrix + notes)
- SOC2_evidence_index.csv (CSV of artifact pointers and Drive links)
- Bridge_Letter_20251106_draft.pdf (Draft bridge letter)

Shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bSOC2_example (permissions: Acme security + AuditCorp)

If AuditCorp wants a dedicated intake, Ellie — can you confirm whether you prefer a CSV manifest + shared folder access or an SFTP exchange? We can accommodate either.

Jordan — if you can confirm which Private features you plan to use (agent/connector vs fully air-gapped on-prem bundle), we’ll mark the guidance accordingly.
